textual_summary: Defence section captures three distinct movements on unmanned systems and GCAP collaboration. Edgewing has been awarded the first GCAP contract, kicking off the trilateral GCAP programme with potential participation by additional nations including India, and the contract covers key design and engineering activities to accelerate momentum and delivery. Separately, the Indian Army unveiled a technology roadmap detailing 30 UAS types and loitering munitions across five categories to guide development and procurement, aiming to mass-produce low-cost drones and strengthen India's drone ecosystem under Make in India / Atmanirbhar Bharat, while stressing greater industry participation from startups, MSMEs and academia. A subsequent report confirms the Army launched a technology roadmap for UAS and loitering munitions, outlining priority areas and providing actionable visibility to industry, academia and research bodies to channel investments, reinforcing a whole-of-nation approach to building a resilient drone ecosystem.

scenes.audio_script: Meanwhile, the Indian Army unveiled a technology roadmap covering 30 types of unmanned aerial systems and loitering munitions across five categories, with the roadmap intended to guide development and procurement of UAS. The plan aims to mass-produce low-cost drones and strengthen India’s drone ecosystem under Make in India / Atmanirbhar Bharat. It emphasizes greater industry participation from startups, MSMEs and academia to advance the drone ecosystem. This roadmap aligns with a coordinated push to scale domestic capabilities and broaden participation in UAS development.
